extraction.segment_function: The prologue introduces the broader human and philosophical implications of modern scientific and technological advancements, specifically the launch of the man-made satellite and aspirations to escape earthly imprisonment, framing these developments as a political question concerning the rebellion against the given human condition.

claims.claim: The immediate reaction to the launch of the man-made satellite was not triumphal pride, but relief regarding the first step toward escaping human imprisonment to the earth.
claims.supporting_excerpt: The immediate reaction, expressed on the spur of the moment, was relief about the first “step toward escape from men’s imprisonment to the earth.”

claims.claim: The question of whether to use new scientific and technical knowledge to alter human existence and escape the human condition cannot be decided by scientific means and is fundamentally a political question.
claims.supporting_excerpt: The question is only whether we wish to use our new scientific and technical knowledge in this direction, and this question cannot be decided by scientific means; it is a political question of the first order and therefore can hardly be left to the decision of professional scientists or professional politicians.

definitions.definition: The very quintessence of the human condition and a unique habitat providing human beings with a place to move and breathe without effort and without artifice.

distinctions.item_a: The human artifice of the world
distinctions.distinction: The human artifice separates human existence from all mere animal environment, whereas life itself remains outside this artificial world and connects man to all other living organisms.

unresolved_context: Details on how political institutions or citizens should address the political questions raised by modern scientific power.
The full scope of the historical transition from secularization to the repudiation of the earth.
must_not_be_lost: The characterization of modern scientific endeavors as an escape from the human condition and earthly imprisonment.
The assertion that decisions regarding the direction of scientific and technical knowledge are political questions of the first order.
